neighbours.label: Punctuation (a period or dash) that closes a comparison introduced by 'like': the point just after the simile, before the writer expands on it
fire: Raising a puppy is like raising a toddler. You never get a full night of sleep.
Writing code is a lot like baking bread – small errors ruin the whole batch.
My grandmother's kitchen smelled like a bakery. Everyone wanted to visit her.
Running a restaurant is just like conducting an orchestra – timing matters more than talent.
He was versatile, like a pocket tool. He could fix almost anything.
Her memory works like a filing cabinet. Every name has its own place.
Getting a visa is rather like climbing a mountain – the last stretch is hardest.
The old bridge swayed like a hammock. We crossed it slowly.
quiet: Raising a puppy takes a lot of patience. You never get a full night of sleep.
Writing code at our company takes many weeks – small errors ruin the whole batch.
My grandmother's kitchen was at the back. Everyone wanted to visit her.
Running a restaurant requires a large staff – timing matters more than talent.
He was versatile and very hardworking. He could fix almost anything.
Her memory has been improving this year. Every name has its own place.
Getting a visa takes about six months – the last stretch is hardest.
The old bridge crossed the wide valley. We crossed it slowly.

notes: Card: broad; peaks on ' –', '.', ',' after 'like a spork', 'like learning process for a student'. Probe: simile + period/dash 0.39-0.55; same punctuation without a comparison 0.06-0.18. Comma after a simile only 0.14, sentence-initial 'Like all teachers,' 0.04, so the period or dash is part of the claim. Arabic and Chinese top examples are not covered.
